model-against-code-at-the-base.text: At the base, the model gives a reject no admission and owes the owner the deposit. The state script refuses a reject until the retraction window has closed, and the request script admits only the processing window or a rejectable request. Payments and the state effect already match. A real phase one rejection was refused on a devnet during ticket 287, and that evidence is kept.

every-caller-of-the-old-rule.text: Every place that encodes the old timing has a disposition: the predicate and its wrapper are deleted, the state and request scripts are repaired, properties and tests are restated, doc comments reworded, the builder's timing filter removed, the conformance interpreter's wait replaced by an explicit placement, CG09 moved to held, and the published pages restated. The builder's existing callers only ever reject expired requests, so they keep their behaviour.

how-far-a-changed-state-hash-reaches.text: Changing the state script changes its hash, and that hash is pinned by hand in the witness script, the naming partition and two envelope fixtures. Through the naming pin it moves the retirement custody and application hashes too. Both manifests are regenerated by their own recipes. Historical evidence that names the old hashes is left as it is.

the-ci-that-already-checks-each-class.text: Each class of failure already has a CI command: the Aiken suites and identities, naming value refusals, the deployed identity check, off-chain lint, build, unit and vectors, the devnet end to end run, the conformance book, the exit and generic rows, the release assembly and root CI. The gate uses exactly those commands.

baseline-at-the-base.text: Root CI at the clean base ran for twenty six minutes and exited one. Every recipe up to the format controls passed. The lint step's workflow linter deadlocked with no CPU use and was stopped after its state was captured. The same linter run directly passed in under a second, and two identical hung linters from other lanes have been on the host for ten days. The failure is the tool, not the repository.
